member.summary:
End-User's locale, represented as a BCP47 [RFC5646] language tag. member.summary: Provides the set of public keys to publish at /.well-known/jwks.json. Implementations decide how keys are stored, rotated, and retired — typically all currently-active and recently-retired (still in token TTL) signing keys are returned, each with a stable kid.

member.name: M:LtiAdvantage.Jwks.IJwksKeyStore.GetPublicKeysAsync
member.summary:
Returns the public keys to publish in the JWKS document.
Rotation guidance: - Always include the current signing key (the one used to sign tokens issued now). - Continue to include each retired signing key for at least the longest TTL of any token signed with it, so verifiers can still validate in-flight tokens after rotation. - Each key MUST have a stable, unique Kid. - Set Use = "sig" and Alg = "RS256" for LTI 1.3 signing keys. - Do NOT include private key material — only the public components (N, E). (JwksControllerBase strips private parameters anyway, as a safety net.)
This is called on every JWKS request that is not served from an HTTP cache. If loading the keys is expensive (database, KMS), cache them in the implementation.

member.name: T:LtiAdvantage.Jwks.InMemoryJwksKeyStore
member.summary: An over a fixed set of keys held in memory.

remarks.para: A reference implementation so that publishing a JWKS does not require writing a store first. It suits a deployment whose signing keys are loaded at startup and rotated by a restart. It is not suitable where keys rotate while the process runs, or where several instances must agree on the current key: implement against whatever the instances share instead.
Keys are sanitized on the way in, so a private JWK handed to this store by mistake is still published as public material only.

member.name: M:LtiAdvantage.Lti.CustomPropertySubstitutions.Add(System.Collections.Generic.IDictionary{System.String,System.String},System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Records a variable's value. Order does not matter: sorts the names longest first, so prefixes such as $Context.id cannot shadow longer names.

member.name: M:LtiAdvantage.Lti.CustomPropertySubstitutions.SubstituteAll(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IDictionary{System.String,System.String},System.Text.RegularExpressions.Regex)
member.summary: Replaces every known variable in in a single pass.
member.remarks: One pass over the original text means a substituted value is never scanned again, so a context titled "$User.id" stays "$User.id" instead of expanding to the user's id. The alternation lists longer names first, so where one name is a prefix of another ($Context.id and $Context.id.history) the longer one wins regardless of the order the variables were recorded in. Names are regex-escaped, and values are inserted through a match evaluator, so neither is read as regex syntax.

member.name: M:LtiAdvantage.Lti.CustomPropertySubstitutions.BuildPattern(System.Collections.Generic.IDictionary{System.String,System.String})
member.summary: Builds one alternation of all recorded variable names, longest first, or null if there are none. Culture-invariant, so case folding matches the ordinal-ignore-case dictionary for ordinary names.

member.name: M:LtiAdvantage.Lti.CustomPropertySubstitutions.CollectVariables
